context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 19 March 1899], Gland, Canton Vaud. Three weeks after the Riviera letters, now stranded in Switzerland as Harold Mellor's guest and bored past bearing. He asks leave to dedicate his next play to Harris, which he did.
quote:
From M. Sebastian Melmoth, Gland, Canton Vaud, Switzerland.

My dear Frank! I am, as you see from above, in Switzerland with Mellor: a rather dreadful combination: the villa is pretty, and on the borders of the Lake with pretty pines about: on the other side are the mountains of Savoy and Mont Blanc: we are an hour, by a slow train, from Geneva. But Mellor is tedious, and lacks conversation: also he gives me Swiss wine to drink: it is horrid: he occupies himself with small economies, and mean domestic interests. So I suffer very much. _Ennui_ is the enemy.

I want to know if you will allow me to dedicate to you my next play, ‘The Ideal Husband’ — which Smithers is bringing out for me in the same form as the other, of which I hope you received your copy. I should so much like to write your name and a few words on the dedicatory page.

I look back with joy and regret to the lovely sunlight of the Riviera, and the charming winter you so generously and kindly gave me: it was most good of you: nor can it ever be forgotten by me.

Next week a petroleum launch is to arrive here, so that will console me a little, as I love to be on water: and the Savoy side is starred with pretty villages and green valleys.

Of course we won our bet — the phrase on Shelley is in Arnold’s preface to Byron: but Mellor won’t pay me! He suffers agony over a franc. It is very annoying as I have had no money since my arrival here — However I regard the place as a Swiss pension — where there is no weekly bill.

My kindest regards to your wife.

Ever Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 32-35 - two bifolia, eight sides on plain unruled cream paper: image 32 shows sides 4 (left) and 1 (right), 33 the inner opening 2-3, 35 sides 8 (left) and 5 (right), 34 the inner opening 6-7. Heading: 'From M. Sebastian Melmoth, Gland, Canton Vaud, Switzerland' - the fourth appearance of the exile name in this folder, and the only one with the 'M.' and the full address. The volume drops it and heads the letter 'Gland, Switzerland'. Emphasis: one underline, '_Ennui_' on side 3 - dark, flat, the width of the word, on unruled paper so there is nothing to confuse it with. The volume italicises it. And it settles the French question the other way again: he underlines 'Ennui' here and 'rien compris' at pp. 1124-1125, but not 'sans le sou' (p. 1123) or 'Rien n'est sacre a un cocher de fiacre' (Ives, p. 1173). The volume italicises all four alike. Only the sheet decides. Null: 'Pension' is not underlined - the volume's italic there is again the French convention, 'Of course' is not underlined either, and the volume prints it roman here; contrast p. 1126, where it is underlined and the volume italicises it. The edition is consistent with the sheet in both directions on that phrase. The title, and a silent correction: he writes ‘The Ideal Husband’ in his own inverted commas, with the quotation mark repeated at the line wrap in his usual way (normalised here). The play is An Ideal Husband. The volume prints 'An Ideal Husband' in italic - so it corrects his article and converts his quotes, neither silently flagged. Sixth instance of the quotes-to-italic conversion in this pass. Another hand: a short vertical annotation reading something like 'Shelley mean', bracketed, at the head of side 8, keyed to the Shelley-Arnold bet. Not identified, and not Wilde's so far as I can tell. Punctuation: his colons carry most of this letter and the volume keeps them, unusually. 1173 - stand, because there the edition read a real difference.
